reasoning: The underlying problem is well-recognized in the AI control literature: the base-rate fallacy / low PPV for rare sabotage is explicitly discussed (e.g. "Monitoring benchmark for AI control" notes that even with low FPR, flagged commands are mostly benign at low prevalence), and audit-budget framing (false alarms reviewed per true catch) is standard since Greenblatt et al. 2024 and the control-protocol-evaluation papers. The proposed two-stage confirmatory screen is also a known control measure — "An overview of control measures" describes an "automated auditing hierarchy" applying increasingly expensive checks before escalating to humans. However, I found no published work that explicitly imports the epidemiology screening-test framework to do a quantitative PPV/NPV sweep across sabotage base rates on published Ctrl-Z/ControlArena sensitivity/specificity numbers and quantifies the two-stage precision gain in those terms; that specific analytic packaging/synthesis appears unexplored, even though all the conceptual ingredients are established.

evidence.title: Monitoring benchmark for AI control
evidence.summary: Explicitly discusses that sabotage monitors must have very low FPR because malicious commands are a tiny fraction of all commands; even with low FPR, flagged hits are far more likely benign than malicious — i.e. the low-PPV/base-rate problem the proposal targets is already articulated here.

evidence.title: An overview of control measures
evidence.summary: Describes an 'automated auditing hierarchy' that applies increasingly expensive (and slow) checks before escalating to human auditors — essentially the multi-stage confirmatory screen the proposal models, treated as a known control measure.

evidence.title: Evaluating Control Protocols for Untrusted AI Agents (2511.02997)
evidence.summary: Analyzes auditing budget, false positive vs false negative tradeoffs, and how safety scales with audit budget; false positives waste audit budget while false negatives let attacks succeed — the audit-budget-per-true-catch economics the proposal would compute are already modeled here.

evidence.title: AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion (2312.06942)
evidence.summary: Foundational control paper establishing suspicion-threshold auditing under a limited audit budget (e.g. audit top 2% suspicion), grounding the precision-at-low-base-rate framing the proposal builds on.

evidence.title: Derivation of Generalized Equations for the Predictive Value of Sequential Screening Tests (2007.13046)
evidence.summary: Provides the exact Bayesian PPV/NPV math for sequential (two-stage) screening tests across prevalence — the epidemiology machinery the proposal would import is fully developed, so the methodological contribution is a transfer rather than a new technique.

evidence.title: Ctrl-Z: Controlling AI Agents via Resampling (2504.10374)
evidence.summary: Source of the empirical monitor sensitivity/specificity numbers the proposal would feed into its Bayes analysis; already studies suspicion thresholds and auditing under budget, the substrate the proposal re-analyzes.
